In [[mathematics]], a '''Weierstrass ring''', named by Nagata<ref>{{harvtxt|Nagata|1975|loc=section 45}}</ref> after [[Karl Weierstrass]], is a [[commutative ring|commutative]] [[local ring]] that is [[Henselian ring|Henselian]], [[pseudo-geometric]], and such that  any [[quotient ring]] by a [[prime ideal]] is a [[finite extension]] of a [[regular local ring]].

==Examples==
*The [[Weierstrass preparation theorem]] can be used to show that the ring of convergent [[power series]] over the [[complex number]]s in a finite number of variables is a Weierstrass ring. The same is true if the complex numbers are replaced by a [[perfect field]] with a [[valuation (algebra)|valuation]]. 
*Every ring that is a [[finitely-generated module]] over a Weierstrass ring is also a Weierstrass ring.
